caption:
My Story 🌿🌸

#usahealth #goodvibes #healtylifestyle #healingjourney
transcript: I received many questions from people asking, where are you from? And why does a Buddhist monk speak English without an accent? It is not very common. So, let me tell you my story. I was born in 1939, in a small village in China. When I was eight years old, during the Chinese Civil War, my family left everything behind. We crossed an ocean and began a new life in a place called Kansas. America gave me safety, but even as a child, I felt I did not fully belong. My father was a doctor, my mother was a holistic healer. From them, I learned two ways of seeing life. How to heal the body, and how to listen to the soul. As I grew older, the noise of the modern world grew louder. The rush, the pressure, the endless wanting. It did not match the life my heart was asking for. At 21, I began questioning everything. Success, time, what it truly means to live well. I stayed in the United States until I was 36. Then, in 1975, during an economic crisis, my wife and I made a choice that many did not understand. With our five children, we returned to China, to a small village called Hongkun. There, for the first time, I understood something important. You can live with very little, and still have everything. But let me tell you this. You do not need to move to China to find peace or happiness. A person lives where their thoughts live. You can stand in the most beautiful place in the world. But if your mind is wandering to dark and restless places, that is where you truly are. And the opposite is also true. When the mind is calm and clear, even a simple life can feel rich and full. If you learn to understand the mind, to guide it gently, no external noise can extinguish its light. I spent many years in a monastery, not to escape the world, but to understand it. I learned that peace is not found by changing where you live, but by changing how you relate to your thoughts. This is not only my story. It is an invitation to return inward, to live gently, and to remember that the quiet strength you are searching for has always been within you.
